tips.comment: A 3 time winner at this C&D, this 8-year-old hails from a stable that is performing well. He recently secured victory in a 7 runner handicap on soft ground, winning by 2 lengths over Rebel Star in a straight forward manner just 13 days ago. Given his positive form, he should continue to be competitive despite a 5lb rise in weight.
Broke his duck at the 18th time of asking when winning over 6 furlongs here in April. Fair efforts in a couple of starts since but is of interest back at this venue today.

Not ready to give up on this horse just yet, even though it's going through a barren run. It's now been 17 runs since its last win last year. It should be encouraged by the LTO effort at Doncaster yesterday. A return back to handicaps, but at a lower mark, might just give her a chance.

Could prove difficult to pass if Mission Classified can get on the front end and get an easy lead. 3rd at Goodwood in May and led for a long way before getting passed, but jockey Hollie Doyle might have a better idea of his ability today.

2-year-old maiden event. Did not get its run here last time out. 3 rivals that ran that day have been entered into class 4 and 2 events, including a rival who was behind that day.
Suggest this horse is better than odds claim it to be
Course and distance winner last time out looks set to win again today. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable going well. Has won five of his seven runs.

Easy win here last month by a good three lengths at the same distance, after switching back to turf for the first time since July last year. Bumped up 6lbs for the win, but current favourite 'Time Patrol' has suffered a bigger jump up over the past three races and may struggle this time around.

The 8yo is capable on his day, win or placed in 18 races. Useful AW form earlier in the year and had an 87 AW mark during March. The return to turf could add a little spark to his running and his turf mark of 72 is very tempting. He is capable on grass, winning as a 6yo off an 87 turf mark.

Has never been the most consistent and was terrible last time in follow-up bid, possibly the race coming too soon. Runs off 5lb higher mark here, but is well in on old form. At the prices, worth an each-way punt.

Twirler was 4th over course and distance 10 days ago. Drops 1lb for that and Nicola Currie on board looks an interesting move. Rode a 40/1 2nd for the stable last week. Decent stall draw in 1 and goes on most ground. Solid each way chance here.

The 8yo is capable on his day, seems in good shape, not beaten far on the AW in his last two runs. He’s had a nice 11 week break and should enjoy the return to turf. He ran a couple of decent races over this 12f trip on fast ground this time last year. He’s weighted to run a big race at this 0-50 classified level.

A winner and runner-up in 3 attempts over course and distance. Disappointed over course and distance in handicap company on penultimate start but could go well at this classified stakes level and won a similar race over course and distance in August 2024.
The 5yo is a previous C/D winner. Two runs this year and his fitness should be fine now. He was a close runner-up 10 days ago, having the measure of the rest. He was rated 8lb higher last summer.

Noble Guest, a 3??'year??'old Mohaather gelding trained by George Margarson, takes his place in the 7f 216y Star Sports Handicap tomorrow at Brighton with David Egan booked to ride??'a strong booking given Egan’s solid current season form .
He arrives off a career-best second at Lingfield on 31 May, finishing just 2¼ lengths behind over 7f 135y, showing marked improvement and winning a photo-finish contest . Prior runs include creditable efforts at Kempton and Newmarket in mid-May, where he raced with intent on good to firm ground .
With Brighton’s undulating mile-uphill finish this seems a suitable test for his staying qualities, and Egan’s tactical nous may help unlock further progress.

Started to find form this season, posting a close 2/5 last time out over C&D, losing by a neck. Runs off the same mark of 62 today, which is also the same mark the horse's only win came at. Great chance. The outside stall at Brighton also seems to get a lot of winners over this trip.

Son of Acclamation, who seems to have improved after wind surgery, having won at Redcar and over course and distance already this spring. Below par at Chelmsford last time, but looks to be a better horse on turf, so should go very well this afternoon.

The 6yo mare is in good shape. Three turf runs this year, a little unlucky in running in the first two of those races before a C/D win in a classified stakes last week, a shade cozy in the end by 1L+ - good RPR rating posted. Now running in handicap company but is still on a handy-looking mark.

A winner over a mile here and making her Brighton 7 furlong debut but is 4 times a winner over this trip on tapeta. Her last 3 runs have all been over a mile here, winning in April, runner-up 17 days later and losing third close to home on the 21st of May. Could welcome the drop in trip here.

EIGHT MILE is a ride for experienced jockey Tom Queally who is 17/85 { 20% } at Brighton which could be a significant pointer. This is a near-basement grade handicap where this racer is well treated and he is double entered also holding a place on Thursday in a handicap at Yarmouth. That is possibly an endorsement of his current wellbeing and he should go well.

ROMAN EMPEROR doesn't find winning that easy but has been steadily improving and stayed on as if he could handle the extra distance last time out. Now drops further in the weights and with two longshots likely to make the running there will be a pace to aim at. This one could be one of the ones that reels them in.
Ilestdancingspirit has had two respectable runs, both in 2nd place, since coming back from a two-year break. He should at least be placed again, provided he does not have to make the running again.

The model I run suggests Banderas can win this one. This result has been driven by Banderas having a comparably high RPR but goes out carrying the same weight as the others. All 9 horses lining up here step out with the same initial amount of weight. Banderas came a decent 3rd last time out only 34 days ago, so comes here in decent form and race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests She Has Notions can cause an upset and win this one. This model result has been driven by She Has Notions lining up with a comparably high RPR but an official rank that's the joint lowest. This subsequently means less weight is being carried over this longer 3m stamina test. She Has Notions carries an initial weight that is just shy of a 2 stone difference to the top weight and market leaders. Freddie Keighly on board relieves a further 10 lbs as a claiming jockey, and that takes the total weight differential to over 2 and a half stone. That is a significant amount over a 3 miles trip. Tries cheekpieces for the first time, and if all clicks, surely the weight difference will be the main story by the finish line.

With trainer Mickey Bowen having a 2 week strike rate of 30% and jockey Sean Bowen a 24% strike rate it's fair to say they are both in fantastic form. Karavomylos makes chase debut today after some fair form over hurdles and managed 2 wins at class 4 level. Should be competitive here.

Cave Article won in April at Hereford and in December at Sedgefield so it's two wins in five races. Trainer Christian Williams has a good record in this race and I do think Cave Article will win the first at Southwell today.

The model I run suggests an outside chance for Fast Deal at 51s is the value bet. This result has been driven by Fast Deal having the highest RPR of the smaller 6 horse race and is very kindly treated in the weights. 2 stone weight difference to the top weight and varying degrees in between around this 3m opener. The reason for the big price is clearly the inconsistency of form and has been pulled up in 3 of the last 6 runs. Surely this risk has to be priced in at 51s. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Flash In The Park can win this one. Flash In The Park lines up with the highest RPR of this smaller 6 horse race. Doesn't look overly penalized for it in the weights and has an official ranking that leaves him joint top with one of the early market leaders. Form is a bit patchy but has placed at Warwick in April over this distance and looks to get on terms here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

I'm going against the favorite Carlton here with Lolaos Du Mou. Carlton is going over hurdles handicapping now and might suddenly become a different beast and bring some of his magnificent AW form with him, but I'm hoping he won't. So Lolaos Du Mou is preferred now with the hood going on again. Won a very good race last time out at Warwick on the 21st of May. Tabitha Worsley rides again.

A tight, small affair in which Brindley is given yet another chance under B. Hughes to get off the mark. A run at Newbury a few outings back was his best but he got worn out at the line. Last time out was a 3rd of 6 result when running here at Southwell for the first time.

Sits 3 lbs below the mark she defied to win over CD last year. Dropping back down to the correct trip this time.
She's won twice over this CD, with both wins coming in the space of 14 days. Both wins were registered last year when she won off that 3 lbs higher mark. She won comfortably also, proving this mark is well within range for her.
She ran a cracker over CD on her penultimate run, just bumping into a well-handicapped horse in Faded Fantasy. Beaten just 2L by the winner. To be fair, she was giving 7 lbs in weight to the winner.
She ran okay last time out. Perhaps found the trip stretching her. She clearly isn't a 3M horse. She was only beaten 6L back in 4th place. That run should tee her up nicely for this race. This looks a very winnable race for her.

Sean Bowen gets the ride on Oneforthefairgreen. She has dropped in the handicap to a new low mark of only 72. The last time Sean rode her, she was 2nd of 8 at Leicester last November. She should be at least placed again, wearing a first-time tongue strap.
Lady's Present fell on her first chase effort recently. As long as she's not unduly affected by that, she has every chance dropped back into this sphere.

Should have finished closer last time, having been set too much to do. But that was a promising effort and on stable debut. More to come from her, and she drops another couple of pounds here. Each-way chance.

Land Girls Luck was going okay when the saddle slipped last time and pulled up. Previous two runs were good efforts (while still learning) and the form has been well franked. Today's trip looks ideal, and the 6-year-old with rider's claim is on a good mark and gets the ground well.

Lily Pearl ran a respectable first race over course and distance in 4th place considering she was drawn wide in stall 10 and was stuck out wide for most of the race. She is likely to do much better this time from stall 3 and should win.
Making her debut here, but looking at the pedigree, she could be in with a shout as she is a half-sister to a horse that did win over this distance.

Henrietta Knight is doing well with her horses, and Educator has been rejuvenated by wind surgery after several mediocre runs over hurdles and one on the all-weather. He has won both runs on the flat since the surgery, both times getting up close to home after being held up at the back over this sort of distance. Oisin Orr takes over from Holly Doyle, but the tactics are not likely to change, and in a five-horse race, traffic problems are not likely at Pontefract.
Lady La Fay is lightly raced and is open to a lot of improvement as she is only a 4-year-old. She likes soft ground, her trainer is in form, and the others have all got question marks in my opinion.

Not often this yard targets the flat, so when they do, it's time to take note. 31 days since Queen Of Steel switched codes and won a Nottingham Class 6 over 16f rather comfortably. Up in the weights because of that, but had plenty in hand and could definitely follow up. Gina Mangan was up last time and comes here for only the one ride.

DIFFERENT DRUM has done much of his running on the all-weather of late but returns to the handicap from a potentially tempting mark here. Forgive the last time out run due to it being the first back from a break. Hopefully, that has served as a tune-up and he's dropped in grade now, so he could get involved.

Yakhabar seems well overpriced here, and I can see this shortening to single odds by tomorrow's off. The good to soft ground will suit, and the increase in distance from his previous race will also help. Runs here on a very low handicap mark.
Three-time course and distance winner. Going no problem. Blinkers back on. Good jockey on board. Shortlist material and should be given serious consideration. Win Bet.

Despite his age, Danzan has proved he retains his ability and looks a contender now dropping in grade, currently ten pounds below his last winning mark. A course and distance winner, he's drawn alongside several slow starters, so I’d expect him to lead or, at worst, secure a good early position, something that could prove crucial. He travelled well for a long way in both starts this term and has been dropped a further 2lb, so he looks a solid each-way player at around 7/1.

The 6yo should be better for his return run two weeks ago, on fast ground and the majority of his rivals were rated 85+ and now facing rivals rated 65-75. He ran to a decent level in his final two starts last year, on slower ground, in class 3 and 2 handicap races while racing off an 8lb higher mark. He can be a big player at this class 5 level on easier ground.

Just one win from 10 runs to date. So far this year, things are not going to plan, but only 2 runs this year and a better effort LTO at Nottingham last month. It should have a better chance with a dropped mark and drop down in class.
Larchill Lass has been coming down in the handicap to a nice mark and is tried here in a first-time hood, so worth a bet at this price.

This horse is a CD winner here in a Class 2 event at a mark of 77. Runs here at 74 with a 7lb claimer on board, taking it down to the lowest since the 2017 handicap debut run. 2 years since the last win, gets its chance today.

Finished 2nd here in class 4 over CD 17 days ago beaten 0.75L . Prior to that won class 5 at Beverley over 5f on good to firm . Drops back into class 5 today with claimer taking 3Lb off , yard have won last 2 renewals of this race .
Runs here for the first time at mark 58 with a 3lb claiming jockey. With conditions to suit, last win at a mark of 70, certainly has each way claims today.

Young Fire ran well two starts ago at Ayr when ridden by Mark Winn in a race that has had a few horses run well subsequently. Last time at Redcar, he was sent off at 4/1 but was never involved. He was against a track bias there, so that run can be forgiven. The angle with this one is the record Mark Winn has when riding. He seems to go much better for this jockey and looks interesting here, a stone below his last winning mark.

The 5yo has 2 wins from 9 on turf. Two runs this year, beaten under a length on quick ground two weeks ago and should be set for a big run. He was a 7L winner last Oct on slower ground. Weighted to go well.

Evelyn's Phoenix produced an improved performance last time out at Redcar after a much-needed reappearance at Beverley and can build on that effort now he's back to his last winning mark. A three-time winner last season, including over this distance, he won’t mind some juice in the ground. Breaking from stall 5, David Allan should be able to secure a prominent position, if not make the running, and he looks a contender in this grade. An each-way shout at around 15/2.
Three runs this year for a new yard, not doing a lot wrong in class 4 and 3 handicap races. More suitable going conditions now for the 4yo, dropping down to class 5 company and down to a handy mark.
Won over course and distance last August from a 3lb higher mark and has been ridden as if she has been building up to something. Drops in class here into a Class 5. NAP BET.

Weakened towards the finish over 7 furlongs at Ayr last time out and likely to welcome the drop back to 6 furlongs, being a winner over this trip off a mark of 77 in April 2024 and races 3 pounds below that tonight.

Won both times here back in October, and returns here at a similar weight and a nice lower draw. Hasn't won at this distance yet, but has placed 2nd three times. Showed improvement at recent Redcar since returning from a break.

Three runs for the 8yo mare this year and is in decent shape. She was a close 3rd of 12 two starts back. She saw the race out nicely last time out, never landing a blow but she met plenty of traffic problems in the final 2f. On a handy mark now, suited by the track and these lower rated rivals don’t look strong.

Highwaygrey loves it here at the track. He's now 9 and could be on the downgrade, but he's worth an interest now down to a class 6, 3 lbs lower than his last winning mark and returned to a track he loves.

Khangai, a 5-year-old gelding by Twilight Son trained by James Owen, tackles the Racing For Everyone Handicap over 1m 2f on tomorrow’s Pontefract card. He’ll be ridden by Kaiya Fraser, whose lightweight claim should help his chances in this big-field event .
Khangai arrives off a solid campaign that includes a smooth victory at Chepstow in June 2023 and consistent midfield efforts throughout this season. He’s finished fourth at Bath (building speed early) and sixth at Brighton on good-firm ground??'comfortably handling the rise in class .
His rating of 56 reflects that he’s not outclassed today, and with Fraser aboard to help conserve his stamina early, he could very well sneak into the places. This trip suits his staying ability, and his strong form profile highlights a horse ready for a big run.
Came a good 3rd 14 days ago over this course and distance and has been dropped 1 lb in the handicap, so sure to have a chance here.

The 7-year-old is in decent shape. Three turf runs this year, a close runner-up on his return. He was beaten 2 lengths 10 days ago. However, entering the final 2 furlongs, he had no room, and the jockey virtually had to stop riding all the way to the line but was still close up at the finish. Good jockey booking for this apprentice riders’ handicap, and he can still claim a useful 7lb.

There are only 7 runners here, so my e/w tip has to come first or second. I believe we have a chance. Cabeza De Llave has won here in the past and has had 3 runs to get fit. Would like a firmer surface but is in with a chance.

EXQUISEMENT has dropped a stone down the weights for three runs in May and has an apprentice taking a further 3lb off. Looks worth chancing at the 66/1 odds currently available with 3 places on offer in this 7-runner race now dropped to 5f.

This R Varian-trained 3-year-old colt can make it third time lucky after being placed in his first two races. The latest was over seven furlongs on good ground at Newbury 24 days ago when coming back from a 307-day break. He kept on well inside the final furlong to finish two lengths in second behind the W J Haggas-trained Raafedd. With Ray Dawson back in the saddle, it looks like a win tonight.

Twice raced gelded son of Frankel & Emulous ( Dam's sire Dansili ) who represents top connections here looked green in his first career start back on the 20th of September 2024 at Newbury to make any impact whatsoever however he showed the benefit of experience on his second outing when last seen at Kempton 217 days ago finishing a nearest finish 5th/12 and shaped better than that bare result suggest he was still obviously in need of the experience however this is a smart gelding that is likely to rapidly improve and is in top nick for this return to action this is the first time we see him racing as a 3yo and he is much better built and should be a lot more professional over on the business end now as a 3yo and is open to plenty on improvment jockey Rossa Ryan takes the ride and can give R Beckett's inmate the perfect return ride here at Windsor son of Frankel must be taken very seriously on his return to action and is likely to be a whole different proposition this season

A decent price for this one, and not surprising given a couple of seventh places so far. But worth considering as both of those runs were in at least two classes above this, so the drop down could see a more competitive run.

This J & T Gosden-trained 3-year-old colt went into a few notebooks the way he won on his racecourse debut over one mile one furlong at Wolverhampton. He ran on strongly in the closing stages to beat his more fancied stablemate Cajole by one length. With improvement expected, he should follow up tonight under Oisin Murphy.

Gregorian's Star has each-way claims. Winner of a bumper in November 2024 and has shown some ability over hurdles (went quite close to winning at Kempton in April). Slowly away when sixth of eight, beaten 18 lengths at Lingfield in recent novice stakes, but entitled to come on for that run 11 days ago and upped to a more suitable ten furlongs trip this evening. Trevor Whelan takes over the reins for trainer Sheena West.

Five career runs for the 3yo filly. She won on her handicap debut during April. Only beaten a head two weeks ago, well clear of the rest. Didn’t have a clear passage - good rating posted. This handicap is not as strong, open to more improvement. Strong jockey change.
Girls Night Out has been well backed here. Still, Aaiden is making a handicap debut, unexposed, and a lot better is expected here than bare form.

Gelded son of Ardad who was last seen at Haydock 17 days ago where finishing 5th/8 however his mark continues to ease and he is now operating on a mark 61 and he can begin to trouble the judge also stepping up in trip tackling the 1 mile 2 furlong trip for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this trip can unlock a whole new level of improvment and seeing he is on a handy mark in a suitable looking assignment I Furtado's inmate must enter calculations jockey S De Sousa takes the ride and can give Space Raider a promising ride here at Windsor

Having raced 3 times, this maiden finished 3rd in a Novice race at Lingfield 42 days ago. She is now making her handicap debut and has the potential to improve. An each-way bet at 25/1 is well worth considering.
Making her debut, but comes from fantastic breeding stock by Frankel and another winning horse over this distance. So everything in favor here to make a winning start.
Gained valuable experience in debut run over C&D when a credible 4th of 14 earlier this month. So will be looking for some improvements, which just might be enough to win this one.

An Oasis Dream filly, a half-sister to the 5f winner Sudden Flight. Her dam was a 6f winner. Trainer Richard Hughes is currently in excellent form and has a strong track record with debutants. The odds of 40/1 present a valuable opportunity for an each-way bet, especially with the added advantage of the jockey's 5lb claim.

Change Signs looks an interesting contender in this sprint. While he has only had one go over 5F in 2024 - finishing down the field - it's worth noting he was very keen that day and likely did too much early. His latest run over 6F here was a much stronger effort, just touched off by Circe, going down a short head after leading and only being collared late. Importantly, he pulled nearly 5 lengths clear of the third, suggesting that was solid form. This is further backed up with Circe finishing a decent 5th at Epsom. Before that, he ran a creditable 6th in a competitive York handicap, and earlier in the year he finished a good 3rd behind Habooba at Kempton. That form has worked out nicely, with Habooba going on to win a decent handicap at York and Epsom 5F winner in behind that day (JM Jungle). He is fairly consistent overall and doesn't seem ground dependent. With dry conditions forecast, the going should suit. Drawn in stall 9, which isn't ideal on paper, but he showed good gate speed from stall 13 last time, so that shouldn't be a major concern if he breaks well again.

The last three races that Regal Envoy has raced in, he has always been partnered by Oisin Murphy. Together, they won two and finished second. One of those wins was over today's course and distance. He has gone up three pounds since his latest win, but with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, he is likely to once again steer Regal Envoy to victory.

Miss Attitude, a 5-year-old Cityscape mare trained by Jack Channon, lines up in tomorrow’s 6f 21y Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap at Windsor. Notably, David Probert, in strong form this season, takes the ride??'a confident booking that suggests she’ll be ridden with intent.
Her recent outing at York (May 31) saw her finish a solid fifth of 13 in the William Hill Top Prices Handicap over 5f, staying on well in midfield on good ground. Prior to that, she claimed victory at Southwell on March 4 and ran commendably through the summer of 2024, including a win at Haydock and placed efforts at Goodwood and Doncaster.
Stepping up to Windsor’s extra 21 yards and with Probert’s tactical nous onboard, Miss Attitude looks primed to target the places in a field suited to her sprinting pedigree. She’s one of those proven types who can surprise at decent quotes when conditions click.

Has the highest mark in this field but was not at his best at Meydan. It's tempting to look elsewhere, especially because the yard has 2 other selections (Michaela's Boy and Fidelius) who are contenders. But Jakajaro is dropping down 2 classes and is good value at the current price.

I can’t be having Regal Envoy or Change Sings here; the former has to shoulder W Knight’s 9% SR (A/E 0.44) with fancied runners when the jockey has 5 mounts that day, meanwhile E Johnson Houghton doesn’t produce decent 5f sprinters (12% SR, A/E 0.46 when fancied). Handicap debutant Miraculous has it all to do off a mark of 99 IMO and I’m not convinced that Miss Attitude is up to winning at this level on evidence of her previous starts. I think an each way play is the way and the one that catches my eye the most is ROSARIO at 14/1. The son of Harry Angel comes out top + blue FlatStats rated and is a consistent sort, winning on his penultimate start at Goodwood. He only beat one home over 6f LTO at Newbury but still only lost by 3.75l and is back down to his preferred 5f today off an unchanged mark. The R Teal yard are having a fantastic season so far (23% SR, A/E 1.85), you’ve got to pay attention when they book C Fallon (22% SR, A/E 1.65) and Teal’s 28% SR (A/E 2.12) with 5f sprinters in C1-3 races adds further confidence.

Woolhampton is a course and distance winner. Was 5th over course and distance 21 days ago and is dropped 1 lb for that effort. On a good mark and is versatile on any ground, so should be capable of a good run here.

The law of sod suggests that the 4-year-old colt 'Law of Average' doesn't have much of a chance based on his last run, 11/11 in a class 1 at Haydock. However, this is much easier, and he has won here before over C and D. So I recommend a small each-way bet on him.
Disappointed last time out when eighth, but fifth at Chelmsford before that is comparable to anything else in this race, so is given the verdict at a decent price.

The 7yo had 2 wins from 8 last year after joining this yard - good RPR ratings posted. He should be better for his return run last month - not given a hard time. Suited by the 12f trip on slow ground. Weighted to go well and the strong jockey booking is positive.

Boston Rover was progressive but remained a maiden over hurdles. He could have needed his first run over fences after a break of 158 days when finishing 2nd at Limerick, where he made a few mistakes, including at the last, after making a lot of the running.

Reserve here, so would need one to drop out, but good price at 16-1. Good trainer, obviously, in Gavin Cromwell. 7lbs claimer up. Two wins from eight over hurdles and has had more experience than many over fences. Started favourite for a handicap chase at Down Royal in December and ran second there. Never really got involved on return at Killarney last month. Useful 7lbs claim by virtue of being a mare. By Jukebox Jury. Possible.

Betty Dutton spent most of its time in distance hurdles, so its chase debut over the minimum looked like a sighter to me. Now back to a distance it could go well at a price, as that last effort was decent. A 50% placer over hurdles bodes well here.

Runcok switches to chasing after a poor run last time over hurdles. But he was highest rated over hurdles, and if he jumps well enough on his first attempt over fences, he should beat the more experienced mare Birdie Or Bust, who gained her first win last time helped by the fall of challenging Out For A Stroll two out at Killarney. She made all there over further.
Best form of these over hurdles, having finished 3rd in the Dawn Run last year, and has the best form of these over fences, where she is likely to be a better chaser. The one to be on here.

The model I run suggests Encanto Bruno can win this one. Encanto Bruno lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the rest of the field but is not overly penalized for it in the weights. All runners go out with a very similar weight to carry around this 2m round trip. Encanto Bruno is one of the few showing form coming into this contest. A decent second 57 days ago and is a previous distance winner, so knows how to get the job done at this distance. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Class hurdler taken well to chasing. Won its last 2 races by over 20 lengths. Looks nailed on here. Ground and trip will suit.

Zenta was a Grade 1 winner over hurdles and won a mares' beginners chase in February, beating her more fancied stablemate Pagane into 3rd place. She could be a danger to Pied Piper, getting eleven pounds not including her rider's three pounds allowance, but she has to bounce back from being pulled up in a Listed handicap chase last month.

The model I run suggests an upset from Minella Sergeant for this one. This result has been driven by Minella Sergeant having an RPR comparable to the others in the field and an official ranking leaving him carrying 10 lbs less than the top of the market and top weight. James Smith on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which brings the total weight carried to the lowest of the 4 runners. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1 pt stake on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by a combination of a small gap back to second in the race simulation but the large value on offer at 41s compared to the win probability % generated by the model.

Willie Mullins has the front two in the betting here with Luckinthecity and Uncle Pat, both on chase debut. But Uncle Pat is coming off a 260-day break since winning over hurdles at Listowel, and Luckinthecity may be the more race-fit for his first chase.
Males Chase debut. Always been thought of as a future chaser, and though he will probably come on for the run, Mullins is more than capable of having one ready first time up.

The model I run suggests Heroes Rise can win this one. Heroes Rise lines up with a comparably high RPR to the rest of the field, and all horses step out carrying the same amount of initial weight. Heroes Rise has Carl Millar on board relieving 5 lbs, which helps over this longer 3m1f trip. Form figures of 82342 and comes back in after a short break. If getting away and running well fresh, can get the job done. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Barry Connell is one of the best at training his horses to change codes - chasing to hurdling or vice versa. Slane Hill made the perfect start to his chasing career 2 years ago when winning his beginner's chase. He has not kicked on but has been over timber for the last year or so. Now, up in trip and back over fences, if he can limit the mistakes and on his preferred good ground, he can go well under Walsh, who has done well in these rider-limited races with two wins.

Mica Malpic was coming off a 529 day break when 7th and well beaten at Tipperary last month over 2m 1f but he did not get a clear run and was not knocked about after his chance had gone. He should appreciate the step up in distance.

The model I run suggests Doran's Law can cause an upset and win this one. Doran's Law is not too fancied by the early market. This model result has been driven by Doran's Law having an RPR comparable to the rest of the field but an official ranking leaving it very well treated at this mark. Goes out carrying the second lowest weight over this longer 3m 1f stamina test with 15 runners. A good second-place finish 35 days ago and looks to build on that here today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This year’s Connacht National looks intriguing, especially with the rain expected to hit the turf in County Roscommon tomorrow. One horse I’m keen to back is Eric McNamara’s 11-year-old veteran, DONKEY YEARS. While he wasn’t terrible in the competitive Killarney National last month, he plugged on steadily over 26f. This son of ROBIN DES CHAMPS drops 1lb for that effort and gets a further 5lb relief thanks to jockey Gary Noonan, who has been in solid form with a 20% place strike rate over the past month. Noonan also boasts a respectable 36.36% place strike rate over the past five years at this track. McNamara, the trainer, has a 26.09% place strike rate recently.
As mentioned, the expected rain should suit this old boy down to the ground, with his best form on ground ranging from yielding to downright swampy conditions. The significant drop in class is another positive. This Old Boy is now 6lbs lighter than his last win over fences and, when factoring in the jockey’s claim, he’s on the same winning mark over hurdles. At 16/1, I think he offers a little hope, enough at least to have a little skin in the game.

AMBITIOUS FELLOW may have been geared up for this specific race as a spring/summer target. He had ace conditional jockey Jake Coen aboard latest retaining the ride and he is well treated as a chaser given his significantly higher hurdles mark. Ground-versatile and a lively outsider.

Only his second start over fences, but I saw enough on his debut. He was jumping well and economically at the rear until jumping too low and upending. But with his good jumping, the ride of Mr. Derek O'Connor, and the increase in trip, it all points towards a positive run.
Blew the cobwebs away over hurdles last time after 5 months off and now reverts back to fences, having won from just a 3 lb lower mark over fences last October. Decent each-way chance.
Oldtown To Emly won a maiden at Ballingarry on his latest run and gets in here with very little weight off a mark of only 76 based on his hurdle performances in 2023 and 2024.

Brian McMahon's 7-year-old gelding, GREAT RAINBOW, may not look like an obvious candidate on paper, but I’m inclined to give him the benefit of the doubt for his debut over fences 18 days ago at Limerick, especially after a 230-day absence. Pedigree-wise, this son of GREAT PRETENDER should be well-suited to both the tough weather and the staying distance. He looked to be staying on well in similar conditions at Ballinrobe (22f) when last seen on heavy ground.
There are a couple of other positive factors. First, the trainer’s recent form, with an impressive 71.43% place strike rate over the past fortnight, alongside a respectable 26.67% place strike rate here at Roscommon over the last five years. Secondly, while jockey Stephen Connor is still classed as inexperienced, he’s in good form, with a 75% place strike rate over the past month and a perfect 100% place strike rate at Roscommon from his two previous rides.
I wouldn’t rush to the bookies, but I’m happy to have a small tentative poke, Given the conditions, trainer, and jockey form, I think he has a sniff.

The model I run suggests an upset by The Eye of Tulla for the last race of the day. The Eye of Tulla lines up for this larger 16 horse race with the highest RPR of any of the runners here. Has been given an official rating of 75, which is the lowest of all the runners and therefore carries the lowest amount of weight on this 3m 1f stamina test. The claiming jockey, Mr. Nugent, picks up the reins and relieves a further 7 lbs off his back, which is valuable over this sort of distance. Not shown signs of form or fluency, but if getting back to potential, can cause an upset. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Looks well handicapped to my ratings after a 3rd over fences at Killarney last time out. The sought-after Sexton in these rider-restricted races takes the reins.

Andyourbirdcansing has only completed once in her last four races, so her jumping is a problem. Her latest was an unseat over hurdles, but over the minimum distance, she could make the running and go close with a clear round off her lowly mark of 90.

Won off 85, 3 runs back in July. Form of that race has worked out well, and he comes here having needed his run 6 weeks ago, from a mark of 91, and has an excellent claimer on top taking 5 lbs off. Excellent each-way chance.

BALTINGLASS HILL is not fully exposed as a handicap chaser and jockey Dylan Robinson has ridden this eight year old previously. Well treated for racing in this sphere and no doubt the Philip Rothwell trained runners are moving much better now. One at decent odds worth considering.

Dreamz is making her chase debut, and while this mare will need to jump better than some of her efforts over hurdles, she should be suited by the good ground. Her best form in bumpers and over hurdles would see her go close if she takes well to the bigger obstacles.
